Class LiveItem

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.item.LiveItem
public final class LiveItem extends Object
One item at an ItemPath, held for as long as a menu stays open on it: a shulker box in a chest, or a bundle in a shulker in a chest. Unlike an ItemRef, which a single write uses up, a live item takes any number of writes, each going back up the chain of containers to the top-level slot, and says when it has gone stale so the menu can close. Get one from ItemSources.live(ServerPlayer, ItemPath). 
LiveItem bundle = ItemSources.live(chest, path);
// The mod's own storage over an item stack, kept in step with the chain:
Storage slots = bundle.storage(new MyBundleStorage(bundle.stack()));
// In the menu: stillValid(player) returns !bundle.isStale()

The item

stack() is one object for the item's whole life, so a storage built over it (one that reads and sets the item's minecraft:container or minecraft:bundle_contents) can hold on to it. At depth 0 it is the live stack in the slot. Deeper, it is a working copy, written up the chain by commit().

Stale

The item is tied to itself, not to its place. It goes stale, for good, when the top-level slot no longer holds the stack it held (the stack moved or was replaced), or, for a nested item, when the item at its path is no longer the item as last read or written: gone, moved, or changed by anything else (another player, a command, a mod). A change elsewhere on the chain (another item in the same shulker box) is read and passed over. A stale item writes nothing.

Close the menu on stale. Have the menu's stillValid return !isStale(): vanilla then refuses the player's clicks into it and closes it on the next tick, so no click lands in a storage that would drop it.

Server side only, on the server thread.
